name: LeRobot SO-101 (SO-100 similar)
actuators: 6x Feetech STS3215 7.4 V bus servos, 1/345 (follower); leader mixes 1/147, 1/191
backdrivable: follower no / leader yes; no force sensing (servo current only)
trick: Leader uses low-ratio (1/147-1/191) servos so it backdrives for teleop; single servo SKU; printed links. Reach/payload are 3rd-party estimates (~0.5 kg max at tuck).

name: Koch v1.1
trick: Stronger XL430 only on the gravity-loaded proximal joints, 18 g XL330 elsewhere: torque budget follows gravity load.

name: PAROL6 (Source Robotics)
actuators: Stepper motors + precision planetary gearboxes / belts
trick: Industrial-style printed arm: steppers + planetary + belts, pneumatic lines routed through arm, CAN + isolated I/O.

name: Annin AR4 (MK5 specs; MK3/MK4 similar)
trick: Machined-aluminium links + off-the-shelf geared steppers. MK3 (RoboDK): 1 kg / 600 mm / 0.2 mm / 10 kg; review found backlash and no closed loop in firmware.

name: BCN3D Moveo
actuators: NEMA 17 steppers (one with 5:1 gearbox), belt reductions, Arduino Mega + RAMPS
trick: Fully 3D-printed structure with belt-reduced steppers: cheapest structure, but low stiffness/accuracy; payload/reach never formally published.

name: Thor (AngelLM)
actuators: 7x NEMA 17 steppers (some 5:1 geared), belts + printed gears
trick: Semi-differential wrist (two small gears acting on a big one) puts both wrist motors in the forearm. 625 mm tall fully extended.

name: Arctos (V2 open-loop kit)
price_kind: non-printed parts kit (+ CAD licence EUR 40-50)
actuators: Stepper motors + belt drives + 3D-printed cycloidal gearboxes, Arduino Mega/GRBL
trick: Printed cycloidal reducers after a belt stage: high ratio and low backlash from printed parts. 2 kg payload is a vendor claim.

name: Hiwonder ArmPi FPV
price_kind: kit w/o Raspberry Pi ($576-754 with Pi)
trick: Eye-in-hand camera + bus servos; education-grade. 0.5 kg 'straightened' payload is a vendor claim.

name: OpenArm (Enactic) v1 / 2.0
price_kind: BOM headline on openarm.dev (scope per-arm vs bimanual unclear); WowRobo OpenArm 2.0 from $6,500
actuators: Damiao QDD: 2x DM-J8009P-2EC (J1-2, 20/40 Nm), DM-J4340P + DM-J4340 (J3-4, 9/27 Nm), 4x DM-J4310-2EC (J5-7 + gripper, 3/7 Nm)
backdrivable: yes / yes (motor current; bilateral force feedback, gravity comp)
trick: QDD (~9-10:1 planetary) + software gravity comp; payload rated at full extension incl. EE (6 kg peak); Al/stainless + printed covers; 1 kHz CAN-FD.

name: AgileX PiPER
actuators: 6 integrated BLDC joint modules (reducer type unpublished), CAN, integrated controller
trick: Controller integrated in base; ~0.36 payload/mass at 626 mm for ~$2k.

name: Trossen WidowX 250 S (discontinued)
trick: Payload only guaranteed to 50% extension - a reminder that hobby-servo payload specs are not at full reach.

name: Trossen ViperX 300 S
actuators: Dynamixel XM540-W270 (waist, 2x shoulder, 2x elbow, forearm roll, wrist) + XM430-W350 (wrist rot., gripper)
trick: 'Shadow' servos: paired motors on shoulder and elbow double torque with one SKU (base of original ALOHA).

name: Trossen WidowX AI (Trossen AI kits)
price_kind: assembled base arm (2026 guide; store $5,935); Stationary AI kit $16-24k
actuators: BLDC joint modules (27 Nm J0-2, 7 Nm J3-5), 24 V, Ethernet/UDP
trick: Same arm SKU used as leader and follower; 1.5 kg rated at full extension.

name: Galaxea A1
trick: 3 kg rated / 5 kg peak at ~0.6 m with ~4 kg arm (payload/mass ~0.7); same arm family on Galaxea R1 (3.5 kg @ 0.6 m).

name: Galaxea A1Z
trick: Cheaper A1 variant: 3 kg rated, 5 kg peak.

name: Berkeley Blue
price_kind: target cost at >1,500 units (prototype BOM $3,328 in 77-unit run)
actuators: iFlight gimbal outrunner BLDC + single-stage 7.125:1 GT3 timing belt; 2-DOF plastic geared differential per link
trick: Belt QDD + per-link differential moves motor mass toward shoulder (~30% less gravity torque and inertia); gripper reuses arm servo; base doubles as heat sink.

name: Pollen Reachy 2 arm
actuators: Orbita 2D (shoulder, elbow) + Orbita 3D (wrist) parallel/differential BLDC actuators
trick: Parallel 2-/3-DOF Orbita joints share motors across axes; internal cable routing. Arm ~662 mm long; docs list 0.5 kg vs datasheet 3 kg.

name: ARX X5 / ARX5
actuators: ARX in-house BLDC joint modules, CAN (EtherCAT-CAN adapter), 500 Hz
trick: Very low mass (~3.3 kg) force-controlled arm used for UMI-style imitation learning. Payload/reach are reseller 'comparable' figures.

name: I2RT YAM (Pro/Ultra/Big variants)
actuators: Damiao DM-series QDD (DM4340 / DM4310; DM4310 or DM3507 gripper), CAN
trick: Motors drop to damping mode after 400 ms comms timeout (safe failure); Pro 3 kg, Ultra 4 kg, Big YAM 4 kg @ 1.1 m.

name: Seeed reBot Arm B601-DM
actuators: 3x DM-J4340P-2EC (J1-3, 27 Nm) + 3x DM-J4310-2EC (J4-6, 7 Nm) + 1x DM-J4310 gripper
trick: Cheapest QDD arm found: CNC 5052-Al core links + printed covers; 1.5 kg at 70% reach w/o gripper (767 mm with gripper).

name: Seeed reBot Arm B601-RS
price_kind: reseller EUR 2,380 incl. VAT (variant labelling ambiguous)
trick: Same open design re-actuated with RobStride 48 V modules: 2.5 kg rated / 5 kg max.

name: UFactory Lite 6
trick: Harmonic drives + controller in base; precise but heavy for its payload (0.075 kg/kg).

name: UFactory xArm 5 Lite
actuators: BLDC servo + harmonic reducer, 17-bit abs. encoders
trick: 5-DOF (one wrist axis dropped) to save cost for top-down picking.

name: Dobot Magician
actuators: Steppers with planetary reducers, all in base
trick: Parallelogram linkages keep the tool level and put all motors at the base.

name: Dobot Nova 2
trick: Entry-level cobot; integrated joints.

name: Elephant myCobot 280 (M5)
trick: All-servo, no external controller (M5Stack/RPi in base).

name: Kinova Gen3 lite
trick: Low power (20 W avg / 100 W peak) - attractive for battery bases.

name: igus ReBeL 6DOF
trick: Injection-moulded plastic gears/housings make it the lightest cobot class (8.2 kg); nominal reach 400 mm.

name: Fairino FR3
trick: Price floor for an industrial-spec 3 kg cobot (~$6k), but 15 kg mass - wrong mass class for a legged base.

name: Boston Dynamics Spot Arm
trick: Whole-body manipulation: body re-poses to extend workspace and add leverage; 11 kg peak lift, 25 kg drag; 5 kg continuous at 0.5 m.

name: Duatic / Dyna-Tech DynaArm (ANYmal)
actuators: Duatic QDD actuators, 48 V, joint torque control
trick: Elbow actuator mounted at the shoulder drives the elbow via a belt, so reaction torque goes to the base; carries ~its own mass (8 kg arm, 6-7 kg continuous; 14 kg for 10 s).

name: Unitree Z1 Air (B1/B2 arm)
actuators: Unitree BLDC + harmonic reducer (60+:1), 33 Nm max, 15-bit enc., RS-485, 1 kHz
backdrivable: low (harmonic) / yes (joint torque control ~0.2 Nm, collision detection)
trick: Designed to bolt onto Unitree quadrupeds; accepts torque/angle/velocity/stiffness/damping commands.

name: Unitree Z1 Pro
trick: Offered as B2 (IP67 quadruped, 40 kg walking payload) manipulation add-on.

name: Unitree D1 (Go2 arm)
actuators: Servo joints, Al alloy body, 60 W
trick: Small arm sized for 15 kg-class Go2 EDU quadruped; 670 mm with gripper.

name: ALMA (ANYmal + 6-DoF torque-controlled arm)
trick: Hierarchical whole-body controller: walk/trot/pace while doing operational-space EE control; torso posture optimisation enlarges the arm workspace.

name: Deep Whole-Body Control (Go1 + low-cost 6-DoF arm)
actuators: Hobby-servo arm (WidowX-250 class, †) on Unitree Go1
trick: One RL policy coordinates legs + arm; legs bend/tilt to extend reach - the legged base is used as extra DOF at ~$6k system cost.

name: Hello Robot Stretch 3
actuators: Closed-loop steppers, belt-driven lift and telescoping arm; servo wrist †
trick: Cartesian lift + telescoping arm: all heavy motors on the base, tiny moving mass; base yaw supplies the missing DOF.

name: Enchanted Tools Mirokai (arm)
trick: Ball-bot base + light tray-carrying arms; 1.5-3 kg per arm reported - specs unverified.

name: FarmBot Genesis XL (Cartesian gantry)
trick: Cartesian gantry over a 3 x 6 m bed with swappable tools via a magnetic universal tool mount †: trivial kinematics, cheap.

name: Small Robot Company 'Dick' (weeder)
actuators: igus delta robot carrying RootWave electric-weeding probe
trick: Cheap 3-DOF delta under the chassis for vertical tool strikes; electrical 'zapping' tolerates mm-level position error.

name: Fieldwork Robotics raspberry harvester
trick: Several cheap arms in parallel + soft gripper; target 25,000 berries/day.

name: Dogtooth strawberry harvester
trick: Table-top crop rows constrain workspace so arms can be simple; ~1/100 berries missed (2023).

name: Traptic strawberry harvester
trick: Arm in an enclosed cart behind a small tractor: controlled lighting, night picking, weather protection for a non-sealed COTS arm.

name: Harvest CROO strawberry harvester
actuators: Rotating 6-claw picking heads; delta robots for packing
trick: Rotary multi-claw heads instead of articulated arms; parallelism (16 heads) for throughput.

name: Saga Robotics Thorvald
trick: Modular reconfigurable chassis; IP rating split by height (submersible parts IP67). UV-C treatment instead of manipulation.

name: Naio Oz (weeding robot)
trick: Passive mechanical hoes on a tool bar - no manipulator needed for inter-row weeding. Robot mass 130-180 kg.

name: Tertill (garden weeder)
trick: Replaces manipulation with a spinning string trimmer under the body; solar-powered; 1.1 kg robot.

name: Ecorobotix ARA (spot sprayer)
trick: Selective actuation of a dense nozzle array replaces a manipulator entirely.
